highlight: caught and corrected its memory pick
device: Linux server running the net-snmp agent
mode: Replay of a recorded live session

pick.evidence: The amount of physical read-write main memory, typically RAM, contained by the host.

evidence.detail: allocated 1024 MiB: change +0 bytes (expected +1,073,741,824 per name rule, ratio 0)

pick.evidence: The amount of physical read-write main memory, typically RAM, contained by the host.

events.reasoning: Live evidence: allocating 1024 MiB caused +0 bytes change on hrMemorySize, proving hrMemorySize (1.3.6.1.2.1.25.2.2) is a static total-physical-RAM scalar that does not track utilization, so it must not be repeated. Switched from total to used: hrStorageUsed is allocated amount per storage pool and will increase with allocation. Filter to device-wide RAM row for physical memory used. Rejected look-alikes: hrMemorySize - failed live test, static total; hrStorageSize (1.3.6.1.2.1.25.2.3.1.5) - also static total size in same table, same failure mode; hrSWRunPerfMem (1.3.6.1.2.1.25.5.1.1.2) - per-process, violates device-wide totals rule; hrStorageAllocationUnits/Descr/Type - metadata not values; Virtual memory/Swap/buffers/cache rows - not device-wide physical RAM. Scale is per-row hrStorageAllocationUnits, typically 1024 bytes on net-snmp Linux, so raw*1024=bytes; poll AllocationUnits column to confirm.

pick.evidence: The amount of the storage represented by this entry that is allocated, in units of hrStorageAllocationUnits.
pick.row_filter: Select row where hrStorageType = hrStorageRam (1.3.6.1.2.1.25.2.1.2), typically hrStorageDescr = 'Physical memory' / 'Real memory'; exclude Virtual memory, Swap, buffers/cache; use same-index hrStorageSize and hrStorageAllocationUnits (typically 1024) to compute bytes = Used * AllocationUnits and percent = Used/Size*100
